detail.title: Experimental and Theoretical Foundations of Prebiotic Heredity
detail.summary: This revision synthesizes the transition from non-templated persistence to heritable evolution, noting the fundamental ambiguity regarding whether evolution requires templated genetic material. Evidence suggests that functional selection can potentially emerge in prebiotic environments prior to the establishment of template-based copying.
detail.reason: Updating to better reflect the distinction between persistent chemical states and heritable evolutionary systems.

detail.summary: Integration of thermodynamic erasure costs into the heredity threshold framework demonstrates that the transition from simple chemical mixtures to evolutionary systems is constrained by both information-theoretic erasure limits and the requirement for objective pointer states.
detail.reason: Revision required to incorporate thermodynamic constraints on information retention and the criteria for objective state persistence.
